service-selection.hint: Two questions decide it: what does the input look like (text, form, image, audio, video, or vectors), and does the job extract/analyze, translate, search/index, or generate? The planted option is almost always the neighbor that shares the input but does the other job.

ss-001.label: Describe invoice fields in plain language and extract them from PDFs, photos, and call recordings into structured JSON
ss-001.why: Natural-language field description over multimodal input → structured JSON is Content Understanding; Document Intelligence prebuilts are deterministic and document-only.

ss-002.label: High-volume deterministic extraction from standard receipts and ID cards with a prebuilt model
ss-002.why: Known form types — invoices, receipts, IDs, business cards — are Document Intelligence prebuilt territory.

ss-003.label: Translate written product manuals from English text into Japanese text
ss-003.why: Translator is text-to-text; Azure Speech handles audio in/out including speech translation — a 6-count corpus confusion (pair #29).

ss-004.label: Index the extracted invoice data so downstream apps can search and retrieve it
ss-004.why: CU extracts; AI Search indexes and retrieves downstream (indexer, skillset, knowledge store) — extraction and retrieval are different services (pair #22).

ss-005.label: Find catalog items whose descriptions mean the same thing as a query, even when the wording differs
ss-005.why: Embeddings convert text into vectors for semantic comparison (text-embedding-3-large) — they retrieve and compare, they never create content (pair #18).

ss-006.label: Answer free-form questions about a photo the user attaches to their chat message
ss-006.why: Image-as-input needs a deployed multimodal model reading image content parts; image generation goes the other direction, and ImageAnalysisClient/Vision returns fixed features — a different API and endpoint (pair #23).

ss-007.label: Read printed text off a photographed street sign so the app can show it back as plain text
ss-007.why: OCR/Read is a core Vision capability over general images; Document Intelligence targets structured form layouts, not incidental street-scene text.

ss-008.label: Automatically detect the source language of incoming text before translating it into English, in the same call
ss-008.why: Translator's language auto-detection runs inline as part of the translation pipeline; AI Language's Language Detection is a standalone text-analytics feature used outside a translation call.

ss-009.label: Train a model on your own labeled photos to tell defective parts from acceptable ones on a production line
ss-009.why: Custom Vision purpose-builds classification/detection from your own labeled images with a managed training loop; general Vision only returns its fixed prebuilt features and can't be retrained on your data.

ss-010.label: Match a badge-scanner photo against a roster of employee photos to confirm the person's identity
ss-010.why: 1:1 verification and 1:N identification against enrolled faces is Face's dedicated capability; general Vision analysis has no identity-matching feature.

ss-011.label: Persist key phrases, sentiment, and entities pulled from a document pipeline into a store downstream apps can search
ss-011.why: A skillset can call AI Language to enrich each document, but the persisted, queryable knowledge store belongs to AI Search — enrichment and retrieval are separate pipeline stages.

ss-012.label: Pull sentiment, key phrases, and named entities directly out of raw support-ticket text
ss-012.why: Sentiment, key phrase extraction, and NER are AI Language text-analytics features; AI Search only consumes that output as an enrichment step, it doesn't produce it.

ss-013.label: Flag an unusual spike in a factory sensor's vibration readings as they stream in over time
ss-013.why: Purpose-built univariate/multivariate anomaly detection over time-series data is Anomaly Detector's job; a general ML workspace would require you to design, train, and manage that model yourself.

ss-014.label: Get a transcript with timestamped speaker turns from a recorded two-person support call
ss-014.why: Speech-to-text with speaker diarization runs directly on raw audio as a Speech capability; AI Language only works on text that's already been transcribed.

ss-015.label: Turn a block of written English marketing copy into narrated audio for a video voiceover
ss-015.why: Neural text-to-speech synthesis is a native Speech capability; producing spoken audio from Azure OpenAI needs a separate multimodal/realtime deployment, and Translator never touches audio at all.

ss-016.label: Flag violent or hateful language in user-submitted chat messages before they ever reach the model
ss-016.why: Prompt Shields and moderation categories are Content Safety's job, applied to input and output alike; AI Language's PII detection is a privacy feature, not a harmful-content classifier.

ss-017.label: Blur or redact a customer's phone number and email address before a chat transcript is stored
ss-017.why: PII Detection and Redaction is a dedicated AI Language feature for spotting and masking personal data; Content Safety instead classifies harmful-content categories — a privacy concern, not a safety one.

ss-018.label: Store and query millions of already-computed embedding vectors so nearest-neighbor lookups return in milliseconds
ss-018.why: Vector search and storage at query time is AI Search's job; Embeddings models only produce the vectors in the first place, they don't index or retrieve them.

ss-019.label: Route a running agent's tool call out to a live weather API and feed the result back into the same conversation
ss-019.why: Invoking a function/custom tool mid-run against a live external API is the Agent Service's orchestration layer; a bare chat completion call has no built-in tool-invocation loop of its own.

ss-020.label: Attach an existing search index to a Foundry agent so its answers ground in and cite your indexed documents
ss-020.why: Wiring a knowledge source into an agent's grounding/citation behavior is configured on the Agent Service; the index itself just serves queries, it doesn't own the agent's persona, tools, or knowledge wiring.

ss-021.label: Generate a photorealistic product mockup image from a plain-English description, with no starting photo
ss-021.why: Text-to-image generation is DALL-E's job; a multimodal chat model reads images as input but doesn't paint new ones, and Vision only analyzes images that already exist.

ss-022.label: Run a cost-sensitive assistant on a budget deployment that only ever handles short, simple requests
ss-022.why: A Phi-class small language model trades some capability for a much smaller footprint and lower cost, which fits lightweight, budget-constrained requests; deploying a full frontier model for simple text is the classic over-provisioning trap.

ss-023.label: Let a user speak a question and hear a spoken answer back in the same low-latency turn, with no separate recognizer/synthesizer calls to wire up
ss-023.why: gpt-realtime / Voice Live is the single low-latency speech-in, speech-out session; the Azure AI Speech distractor means wiring up the manual SpeechRecognizer→process→SpeechSynthesizer pipeline yourself, which loses on latency and integration — exactly what the realtime API replaces.

ss-024.label: Get the deployed model's reply back as well-formed JSON matching a schema you supply, with no extra prose around it
ss-024.why: Structured output is a per-call parameter on a deployed chat/completion model; fine-tuning permanently changes model weights and is unnecessary just to shape one response's format.

ss-025.label: Bake a company's writing style into every future response using hundreds of labeled example transcripts, so it never has to be re-prompted
ss-025.why: Fine-tuning is the training pass that bakes demonstrated behavior into new weights so it persists across calls; a stock chat/completion deployment only reflects what's resent in that call's prompt, and a multimodal model changes what input types are accepted, not whether style persists without re-prompting.

ss-026.label: Try out voice input on an audio-enabled model deployment from the Foundry chat playground, with no code involved
ss-026.why: An audio-capable multimodal deployment can be exercised straight in the chat playground; Voice Live/gpt-realtime is the dedicated low-latency realtime session API, a separate deployment path built for continuous conversational voice.
